newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Guterres says EMU candidacies must be on merit.
newsitem.headline: Guterres says EMU candidacies must be on merit.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Tuesday that single currency membership must be decided on a country's own merits, with no regard for the performance of its neighbours within the European Union.
The Socialist leader mentioned no names but the reference was clearly to Spain and Italy, often lumped together with Portugal as the so-called 'Club Med' countries.

"What is being tested is the (economic) performance of each country and not that of its neighbours," Guterres told central bankers attending a ceremony to mark the 150th anniversary of the Bank of Portugal.

"It would be completely unacceptable if instead of the decision (on EMU) being taken by political leaders it were taken by a sort of travel agency...based...on the various resorts of the Club Mediterranean," he said.
"(This) would be violation of the sovereignty of individual European Union) members," he said.

Guterres, whose government has made qualifying for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) its top policy priority, said that the only thing that counted was whether an individual country met the conditions laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
Entry to EMU demands that a country meets certain economic criteria, on the budget deficit and inflation amongst others, in 1997 ahead of the single currency's launch in 1999.
